targets.approach: Start from the Red Pine trailhead and go up into Maybird Gully past the Maybird lakes, then head southwest to the notch into Hogum Fork. Cross a long stretch of boulders and talus west toward the head of Hogum Fork. When Thunderbolt Ridge comes into view, climb one last hill into the cirque. Stay close to Thunderbolt Ridge, and Cloud Wall is the first clean rock on the west-facing wall. The route is the furthest left on the wall.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the bolted belays; every route on the wall has them.
targets.name: Laputa

targets.approach: Start from the Red Pine trailhead and go up into Maybird Gully past the Maybird lakes, then head southwest to the notch into Hogum Fork. Cross a long stretch of boulders and talus west toward the head of Hogum Fork. When Thunderbolt Ridge comes into view, climb one last hill into the cirque. Stay close to Thunderbolt Ridge, and Cloud Wall is the first clean rock on the west-facing wall. The route is the furthest right on the wall and finishes on top of Thunderbolt Ridge proper.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the bolted belays; every route on the wall has them.
targets.name: Orographic Lift

targets.approach: Drive up Little Cottonwood Canyon as far as possible and continue to the Albion Basin Campground. A trail leaves from campsite 13 and passes some private homes; stay on it, and above the trail and treeline the way to the north face of Devil's Castle is obvious. The route begins close to the left of Gothic Miller.
targets.descent_text: Walk off. Routes on the Castle are normally walked off.
targets.name: Enemy at the Gate

targets.approach: Drive up Little Cottonwood Canyon as far as possible and continue to the Albion Basin Campground. A trail leaves from campsite 13 and passes some private homes; stay on it, and above the trail and treeline the way to the north face of Devil's Castle is obvious. The route lies west of Portable Darkness on the large black streak, its bolts visible from the ground, and the line climbs an ear-shaped feature.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route from the belay anchors.
targets.name: Poon Limp or Eat Crust

targets.approach: Drive up Little Cottonwood Canyon as far as possible and continue to the Albion Basin Campground. A trail leaves from campsite 13 and passes some private homes; stay on it, and above the trail and treeline the way to the north face of Devil's Castle is obvious. The route is at the beginning of, and to the left of, the Horns of Satan gully; if you are in the gully you have gone too far.
targets.descent_text: Walk off. Routes on the Castle are normally walked off.
targets.name: Touch of Grey

targets.approach: Distant Drum is a remote, shady stretch of cliff beyond the Lower Jungle, split into the Commuter's Wall of shorter routes and the Village Wall of longer ones. Cairned trails drop to the base from the road and from campsites above to the northwest; they have fixed hardware to assist, but no rappel is needed. It sits immediately left of the shorter crack called Congolese Crescendo, with the face between them a good top-rope.
targets.name: Running Around the Bush

targets.approach: From the main Brighton Lodge, hike up the Lake Mary trail and keep to the well-worn path to the Dog Lake junction, where you turn left. Either way around Dog Lake reaches the slab; the right-hand side avoids some swampy ground. The route starts at the bottom-most toe of the prominent slab, where there is a flat belay area at the base.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the chains at the top.
targets.name: Best in Show

targets.approach: From the main Brighton Lodge, hike up the Lake Mary trail and keep to the well-worn path to the Dog Lake junction, where you turn left. Either way around Dog Lake reaches the slab; the right-hand side avoids some swampy ground. It begins right beside Best in Show on the right, follows a seam running right to left, and crosses that route before continuing left to its own anchor higher up.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the chains at the top.
targets.name: The Pug

targets.approach: Eardley Canyon is south of the last developed climbing in the San Rafael Swell: from the junction of I-70 and Highway 24 go south to a westbound dirt road, follow it to where it ends at the mouth of the canyon, then walk up the wash to the climbs, which are all a short way up from the end of the road. From Huntsman Tower walk west, then south to the back of the alcove; the right-facing corner is visible from the wash.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the bolts on the ledge at the top.
targets.name: Another Birthday Butt Crack

targets.approach: Eardley Canyon is south of the last developed climbing in the San Rafael Swell: from the junction of I-70 and Highway 24 go south to a westbound dirt road, follow it to where it ends at the mouth of the canyon, then walk up the wash to the climbs, which are all a short way up from the end of the road. Look for Belnap Buttress on the wash's north side; from Huntsman Tower, glance north up the talus field. The climb is at the back of the buttress.
targets.name: Back Door Crack

targets.approach: Eardley Canyon is south of the last developed climbing in the San Rafael Swell: from the junction of I-70 and Highway 24 go south to a westbound dirt road, follow it to where it ends at the mouth of the canyon, then walk up the wash to the climbs, which are all a short way up from the end of the road. The route is the upper section of Huntsman Tower, with belay bolts at its base; get there by scrambling up the slope east of the tower's base, which includes a short third-class traverse.
targets.name: Dyslexic Swell Stone

targets.approach: Eardley Canyon is south of the last developed climbing in the San Rafael Swell: from the junction of I-70 and Highway 24 go south to a westbound dirt road, follow it to where it ends at the mouth of the canyon, then walk up the wash to the climbs, which are all a short way up from the end of the road. The route is on the right side of Huntsman Tower. Get there by moving across from where Dyslexic Swell Stone begins and rounding the third-class corner to the large ledge at the base of the climbing.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the bolts at the top of the tower.
targets.name: Hanging with Hadden

targets.approach: Eardley Canyon is south of the last developed climbing in the San Rafael Swell: from the junction of I-70 and Highway 24 go south to a westbound dirt road, follow it to where it ends at the mouth of the canyon, then walk up the wash to the climbs, which are all a short way up from the end of the road. Huntsman Tower is the prominent buttress with a semi-detached tower, half a mile up the wash; its bolts are visible from the wash.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route in several rappels.
targets.name: Huntsman Tower

targets.approach: Eardley Canyon is south of the last developed climbing in the San Rafael Swell: from the junction of I-70 and Highway 24 go south to a westbound dirt road, follow it to where it ends at the mouth of the canyon, then walk up the wash to the climbs, which are all a short way up from the end of the road. From Huntsman Tower follow the wall around the corner to the west, then south up the valley; the pine tree beside the route is visible from the wash.
targets.name: Irv’s Crack

targets.approach: Eardley Canyon is south of the last developed climbing in the San Rafael Swell: from the junction of I-70 and Highway 24 go south to a westbound dirt road, follow it to where it ends at the mouth of the canyon, then walk up the wash to the climbs, which are all a short way up from the end of the road. The route is just to climber's left of Another Birthday Butt Crack, taking the obvious crack system to the top of a large ledge.
targets.descent_text: Nothing is fixed at the top. Walk off eastward from the far end of the ledge, rather than down the first ravine.
targets.name: Jared Has 9 Lives

targets.approach: Find the climbers' trail just east of the Highline trail parking lot and follow it to the base of the main Iron Hayden wall. Traverse north along the base until a short rocky ridge blocks the way, descend a short distance, and keep traversing the base of a short wall into the Hayden Couloir. Cross over the couloir to the skyline arete, then scramble up to its base. The route is on a tower formation a short way right of Estwing Arete.
targets.name: Sultans of Slander

targets.approach: No trail leads to Flamingo Wall in Big Cottonwood Canyon, and none is expected. Easy fifth-class climbing leads up to the first ledge, from which most routes start. The route starts in the middle of that ledge at a pair of cracks that converge into one, marked by a rock placard.
targets.name: Albert N’ Sons

targets.approach: No trail leads to Flamingo Wall in Big Cottonwood Canyon, and none is expected. Easy fifth-class climbing leads up to the first ledge, from which most routes start. The route starts on that ledge at its right side, at a rock placard, up a thin seam.
targets.name: Slot Machine

targets.approach: Park a little beyond the Upper Canopy parking and its white cairn, where the road swings north. An old logging and cell-tower road leaves on the west side, with berms across its entrance; walk it along the cairns to a big cairn set on a stump, then turn south-southeast onto a short forest trail to the cliff edge, and find the cairned way down through loose ground, helped by via ferrata hardware and a fixed line. The route is close to Kestrel Tower, on the main wall immediately right of The Pink Flamingo, reached after a short chimney pitch to a high ledge.
targets.descent_text: Lower off the anchor's quick-link to either the ledge or the canyon bottom.
targets.name: Alpine Nutcracker

targets.approach: Gates of Hell Buttress is a big west-facing buttress, well to the right of the ice route Stairway to Heaven, gray limestone below and beige sandstone above. Park at the lot about half a mile west of the Bridal Veil Falls parking lot, then bushwhack and climb scree to a large alcove below the centre of the face.
targets.name: Gates of Hell

targets.approach: Park at the first, smaller hiker lot at the Highline Trail parking area, then head east-southeast across fairly flat ground, not on the Highline Trail itself, following cairns and staying high. That reaches the top of the cliff at Black Streak Wall; hike east from there past the Cave Buttress Wall, crossing a wooded slope, to the Exposure Arete Wall, a broad face carrying a jagged right-facing arete. The route is to the right of Exposure Arete, through the roof on its left side, left of Organ Harvest.
targets.name: Hail & Hearty

targets.approach: Park at the first, smaller hiker lot at the Highline Trail parking area, then head east-southeast across fairly flat ground, not on the Highline Trail itself, following cairns and staying high. That reaches the top of the cliff at Black Streak Wall; hike east from there past the Cave Buttress Wall, crossing a wooded slope, to the Exposure Arete Wall, a broad face carrying a jagged right-facing arete. The route starts a short way right of Purple Gerbil, up the right edge of two successive flakes.
targets.descent_text: Come down by rappelling or lowering from the anchor on Exposure Arete.
targets.name: Passive Aggressive

targets.approach: Lone Peak Cirque is a long, steep hike, made from the Peak View trailhead on the Jacob's Ladder route. Hyperform Wall is the first wall reached after the long slog, before rounding the bend into the cirque proper. The route is at the right end of the wall, below two green dihedrals and a green and brown patina face.
targets.name: Green Corner

targets.approach: Lone Peak Cirque is a long, steep hike, made from the Peak View trailhead on the Jacob's Ladder route. Hyperform Wall is the first wall reached after the long slog, before rounding the bend into the cirque proper. The route is on the right side of the wall, in a major corner system, to the right of a patina face.
targets.name: Walk The Plank

targets.approach: From the Upper Jungle, drive north on the main road past the Dark Continent parking to a road on the left, at a cell-tower box marked 11, and take Forest Service Road 1458 past a cell tower, then turn right onto a logging road that runs northwest to a pull-out with a large cairn. A re-cut trail leads to the cliff edge, where an easy down chute has a fixed line. The route lies at the right-hand end of the polished face, directly right of Talus Knirschen, and uses the same anchor.
targets.name: Dads, Dogs, and Kids

targets.approach: Lone Peak Cirque is a long, steep hike, made from the Peak View trailhead on the Jacob's Ladder route. All routes on Question Mark Wall are reached by Pete's Staircase, a wandering line that gains the ledge from which the routes begin. The route has the same start as The Right Question, then traverses left from that route's higher belay and finishes by joining the Question Mark Wall Route.
targets.descent_text: From the top of the wall, go east and down the ramp that leads back onto the ledge.
targets.name: Questionable Connection

targets.approach: Lone Peak Cirque is a long, steep hike, made from the Peak View trailhead on the Jacob's Ladder route. All routes on Question Mark Wall are reached by Pete's Staircase, a wandering line that gains the ledge from which the routes begin. It starts to the right of the Question Mark Wall Route, below a few small green corners that face right.
targets.descent_text: From the top of the wall, go east and down the ramp that leads back onto the ledge.
targets.name: The Right Question

targets.approach: From the lower Jungle parking, drive on to the meadow, turn left into it and follow the two-track to the parking at the top of the valley. Walk the old logging road left of a fence southeast through a short stretch of dense deadfall, take the first break on the left (small cairn), and follow it to a primitive trail on the right that leads to the cliff's edge. A cairned trail runs southeast to the crag, with the north entrance marked by two cairns. The route starts in the big red corner.
targets.name: Anti Star

targets.approach: From the lower Jungle parking, drive on to the meadow, turn left into it and follow the two-track to the parking at the top of the valley. Walk the old logging road left of a fence southeast through a short stretch of dense deadfall, take the first break on the left (small cairn), and follow it to a primitive trail on the right that leads to the cliff's edge. A cairned trail runs southeast to the crag, with the north entrance marked by two cairns. The route is a short way right of the Mini (Little) Mesa, the next line right of the face corner and just left of the chimney.
targets.name: Here and There

targets.approach: From the lower Jungle parking, drive on to the meadow, turn left into it and follow the two-track to the parking at the top of the valley. Walk the old logging road left of a fence southeast through a short stretch of dense deadfall, take the first break on the left (small cairn), and follow it to a primitive trail on the right that leads to the cliff's edge. A cairned trail runs southeast to the crag, with the north entrance marked by two cairns. From the south entrance, walk the long cliff for a short way to the obvious crack line with wedged blocks.
targets.name: Surf Swag

targets.approach: Past Mount DeMoisy at Snowbasin's south end, the Hogs Back is a rib made of stacked low-angle slabs. Reach it from the gondola or the Needles Lodge by following the road south toward the DeMoisy chairlift, then the road past the top of the Strawberry gondola, which turns north and then south again to the base of the formation. The route begins where the Hogs Back is lowest and runs up its middle.
targets.name: Hogs Back Proper

targets.approach: The Sisters are reached from the Snowbasin gondola by walking up to the DeMoisy chairlift's top terminal and carrying on south on the road to a sharper turn, where talus begins. At the talus turn left and drop to the lowest face of the Sisters; a bit of bushwhacking and scree gets you to the foot of the route.
targets.name: Standard East Face

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Bald Mountain trailhead and hike the Notch Mountain trail up to Notch Lake. Swing north around the lake, then push northwest through the trees to a talus field, which leads to the foot of the buttress's east side. The route is on the higher tier a short way to the right of Hall of the Mountain King, below a giant triangular roof with a zigzagging flake about two-thirds of the way up; a carved plaque set at the bottom shows where to begin.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route, using the rappel station above the trees as well.
targets.name: 40 lb Mustache

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Bald Mountain trailhead and hike the Notch Mountain trail up to Notch Lake. Swing north around the lake, then push northwest through the trees to a talus field, which leads to the foot of the buttress's east side. The route starts a short way left of the access pitch used by the other three routes on the central column, at a bolt on a chossy pedestal.
targets.descent_text: Rappel from the bolted belays, which are equipped for it; pull the ropes slowly, since they can dislodge loose rock.
targets.name: Caveman Tactics

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Bald Mountain trailhead and hike the Notch Mountain trail up to Notch Lake. Swing north around the lake, then push northwest through the trees to a talus field, which leads to the foot of the buttress's east side. The route is a short way right of the corner approach pitch to the central-column routes, beneath a big pillar that has an upside-down cross in the sandy rock near its top; scramble up some choss to the sandy, shrub-covered area under it.
targets.name: The Debacle

targets.approach: Leave the car at the Bald Mountain trailhead and hike the Notch Mountain trail up to Notch Lake. Swing north around the lake, then push northwest through the trees to a talus field, which leads to the foot of the buttress's east side. The route starts at the same place as Hall of the Mountain King, but wanders up the blocky wide break on the left side of the bolted slab and its roof.
targets.name: The Jester

targets.approach: Upper Jungle is the pair of cliff bands, east and west facing, on the road above the Lower Jungle parking. Park on the right, continue around the corner up the road to the marked Upper Jungle, and follow the short, cairned approach down to the crag. The route starts up a thin crack to the right of Great Ape Escape and Goodall Times.
targets.name: Dorothy's Flying Monkeys

targets.approach: Upper Jungle is the pair of cliff bands, east and west facing, on the road above the Lower Jungle parking. Park on the right, continue around the corner up the road to the marked Upper Jungle, and follow the short, cairned approach down to the crag. The route starts up a thin crack to the right of Great Ape Escape and Goodall Times.
targets.name: Monkey Man

targets.approach: The tier is reached from the Trial Lake area: cross the dam on the west side and follow the trail along the lake to Wall Lake, or use the Wall Lake trailhead near Crystal Lake. Work around the lake's left side beyond the main lower tier, then cross a meadow to the upper tier. The route is right of Upside Surprise, up a finger and hand crack through a roof.
targets.name: Raising the Roof
